source.title: VeLU: Variance-enhanced Learning Unit for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Ashkan Shakarami; Yousef Yeganeh; Azade Farshad; Lorenzo Nicolè; Stefano Ghidoni; N. Navab

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no document problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: It compares held-out classification accuracy for several optimizers, a different measure of optimizer generalization performance than the claim versions' training-to-test gap.
record.gate_note: Only the optimizer comparison in Table 6 bears on a listed version. The activation-function comparisons and validation-loss curves do not report the training-to-test gap, and the paper does not compare convolutional with fully connected networks or evaluate dropout, memorization, width sweeps, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: Table 6 compares optimizer-specific held-out classification accuracy in a new VeLU setting, bearing on V4. V4 does not require a training-to-test gap measurement. The optimizer tuning protocol is unspecified, so correspondence to its limited-tuning condition remains uncertain.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimizer subsection: the authors interpret the results as effective training across optimizers, with Adam highest in top-1 accuracy. Their overall conclusion is that VeLU improves accuracy and stability across CNNs and ViTs with one learnable parameter and modest overhead. Table 6 alone does not establish their additional assertion that VeLU improves performance under every optimizer, because optimizer-matched non-VeLU baselines are absent.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares optimizer-specific accuracy using VeLU on one ResNet50 image-classification setting; it does not measure the training-to-test gap central to the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported top-1 accuracy varies across the four tested optimizers; Adam is highest.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation comparisons report improved accuracy and validation-loss trajectories with VeLU across CNNs and ViTs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing activation functions can improve held-out image-classification performance and convergence.

record.problems: Table 6 reports accuracy without uncertainty, does not specify the evaluation split in the table, and provides no corresponding training accuracy or loss for the optimizer comparison; therefore it cannot establish a generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Whether tuning was restricted to learning rates and schedules; corresponding training performance; broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; language tasks.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout addition or removal, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Identifying and removing memorized examples, followed by retraining.

missing.what: Table 6 also reports top-5 accuracy: Adam 99.70%, SGD 99.70%, Nadam 99.19%, RMSProp 99.03%. Adam's advantage therefore depends on the accuracy metric; the other two adaptive methods remain below SGD.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Table 6 gives no uncertainty or optimizer-specific learning rates, schedules, or epoch counts. Section 3's identical-hyperparameter statement concerns comparisons across activations and does not establish a controlled optimizer-tuning protocol. Figure 4 depicts activation output landscapes, not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity analysis.
No comparison of training performance, broader hyperparameter tuning, weight decay, optimizer switching, or language tasks.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch analysis.
No dropout or weight-decay removal/addition comparison.
No sharpness, norm, margin, or training-to-test-gap measurement.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-1 accuracy using VeLU with Adam.
rows.note: The paper reports optimizer-specific accuracy, but does not state in this table whether this is test accuracy or give training performance for the comparison.
rows.check: Use SGD's 89.33% as the comparison baseline: Adam achieves 91.32%, an advantage of 1.99 percentage points. Section 3 describes benchmark evaluation splits, supporting a held-out interpretation despite Table 6 not naming the split. Training performance is unnecessary for this comparison.
